atoms.name: Fetch and micro-operations
atoms.one_line: Fetch: MAR ← PC; MBR ← M[MAR] (with PC ← PC + 1); IR ← MBR. Micro-operations show direction and order.

atoms.name: Datapath sequencing
atoms.one_line: One bus carries one value per step; operands wait in holding registers (Y, Z); order follows data dependence.

atoms.name: Hardwired control
atoms.one_line: Control signals are gate logic of opcode, step and flags. Fast, hard to change, typical of RISC.

atoms.name: Microprogrammed control
atoms.one_line: A control store holds microinstructions; each machine instruction has a microroutine. Flexible, slower, typical of CISC.

atoms.name: Horizontal vs vertical microinstructions
atoms.one_line: Horizontal: one bit per signal, wide, parallel. Vertical: encoded fields, narrow, needs decoders.

atoms.name: Control word and store size
atoms.one_line: Width = sum of fields; words = 2^address bits; size = words × width.

atoms.name: Micro-sequencing
atoms.one_line: μPC, next-address field, condition-select MUX of ceil(log2 conditions) bits, opcode mapping ROM.

atoms.name: Field encoding
atoms.one_line: Mutually exclusive signals share a field of ceil(log2(k + 1)) bits, including a code for none.
